notes: Commerce Dept finalized CHIPS and Science Act R&D award to Anderon, a newly formed IBM subsidiary running a 300mm pure-play quantum wafer foundry in Albany NY. Converts the May-2026 letter of intent into a definitive agreement. IBM matches with $1B cash plus IP/assets/workforce. Per GovConWire (corroborating), Commerce takes a minority non-controlling equity stake as a condition of the award; disbursed over ~5yr tied to milestones.

Commerce Dept finalized CHIPS Act R&D award (up to $375M) for a secure domestic quantum foundry plus cryogenic CMOS / advanced packaging R&D. Disbursed over 5yr tied to milestones. Distinct from GlobalFoundries' earlier, much larger $1.587B manufacturing-capex CHIPS award for its NY/VT fabs - do not conflate the two.

Commerce Dept finalized definitive CHIPS Act agreement (up to $100M), converting a May-2026 letter of intent. Per D-Wave's own BusinessWire release (corroborating), Commerce receives a minority non-controlling equity stake as a condition of funding; secondary reporting (unconfirmed on the NIST page itself) describes an initial ~$53.6M tranche with the remainder milestone-gated.

Commerce Dept finalized CHIPS Act R&D award (up to $100M) for superconducting quantum computing work (readout electronics, cryostats, high-connectivity chip fabrication). Part of the same Sept-8 batch of quantum CHIPS finalizations as GlobalFoundries, D-Wave, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum.

Commerce Dept finalized CHIPS Act R&D award (up to $100M) for photonic quantum computing R&D (electro-optic materials, single-photon detectors, photonic packaging). Part of the same Sept-8 batch as GlobalFoundries, D-Wave, Rigetti, Quantinuum.

Commerce Dept finalized CHIPS Act R&D award (up to $100M) for trapped-ion quantum systems (integrated photonics, cryogenic semiconductors). Part of the same Sept-8 batch as GlobalFoundries, D-Wave, Rigetti, PsiQuantum.
